question: What independently supplied information can identify a variable-length substitution rule, rather than merely place the answer among alternatives? Compare no hint, unlabelled code-group boundaries, and aligned known plaintext words. No language score is used.
motivation: Phase27 invalidated a narrow positional bijection comparison, while reversible nulls also escaped that comparison. Phases28/29 expose unit and null ambiguities. This motivates testing broader variable-length codewords with external constraints, not claiming that this is the Voynich encoding. Earlier manuscript alphabets, marginalia and zodiac annotations provide candidate evidence to audit, not trusted plaintext pairs.
development: Only synthetic seed9 examples use the26 fixed reference words before freeze. Four exposed phase28 cases remain labelled regressions; their earlier answers and keys are known to the operator and excluded from every new-data gate. Their new hints are simulated from their known generation keys, not newly discovered manuscript evidence.
timing: Freeze source snapshots and preparation, all source ranges, reference words, hint doses, corruption rules, code, seeds, metrics and stop rules before new controls and measurements. Source acquisition and availability counts are allowed beforehand. Local freeze, not external preregistration or human blinding.
encoding_model: One fixed injective prefix-free codeword of1..3 ciphertext glyphs per a-z plaintext letter, known word spaces. Optional constant word-final padding of0..2 glyphs, allowed to reuse glyphs from codewords. Optional reversal of each entire encoded word, including padding. Direction, codewords and padding unknown. Ciphertext alphabet0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ; generated new codes use its first12 glyphs. No language model, frequency score, translation lexicon or assumed source language enters inference. Proper normalization defines a-z benchmark plaintexts; that alphabet is not established for Voynich.
new_sources: New downloaded public-domain Collodi Pinocchio (Gutenberg52484, Italian) and Voltaire Candide (Gutenberg4650, French), raw source/license retained. Sources start at first narrative text, remove chapter headings/summaries, illustration captions and numbered footnote paragraphs; preserve original bytes separately. NFKD, drop accents, expand oe/ae ligatures, lowercase a-z tokens; punctuation/apostrophes become supplied spaces. Exact preparation frozen. No claim that these works represent medieval languages.
partitions: Two source pairs per author:500 fit words starting4000 and8000, gap100,200 transfer words. First2000 source words reserved only for Markov generation. All eight literary intervals and each generation reference disjoint within source. Four underlying literary pairs, not independent replications for each encoding or hint condition. Total2000 fit and800 transfer literary words before duplicated variants/artificial genuine-final modification.
positive_cases: Four literary pairs times4 new encodings:26 random distinct digraphs; random prefix-tree codewords of length1..3; variable code plus constant two-glyph padding; same with whole-word reversal. Four additional no-null adversaries append a genuine plaintext a to every word before variable-code encryption, including their aligned reference and validation words. The a belongs to the plaintext and must be recovered, not removed.20 positives; codewords/keys newly generated. Same base passages across variants, distinct specified keys.
other_cases: Eight outside-model cases: each base pair with alternating codewords per repeated-letter occurrence within a word (homophonic), and with26 distinct four-glyph codewords. Two Markov word-sequence controls generated from each author's reserved initial2000 words, with variable code and padding. No chosen literary passage; may inherit real words. Plus four exposed phase28 regressions.30 new cases and4 regressions total.

hints.none: Ciphertext alone. Construct two explicit prefix-code countermodels by relabelling, if possible. No language or meaning-based tie-break. Inability to construct the cheap certificate is abstention, never recovery.
hints.groups: For every fit word supply the partition into genuine codewords and a padding chunk if present, in visible order, WITHOUT identifying which chunk is padding or assigning any plaintext letters. These are synthetic oracle code-boundaries, a much stronger observation than merely seeing a paleographic ligature. No transfer groups supplied. Keep feasible unlabelled structures and demonstrate at least two label permutations; no plaintext release.
hints.word: No group boundaries supplied. Provide first1,4,12,26 aligned words from the fixed modern NATO alphabet list, normalized xray, alfa, juliett. This is a modern experimental reference catalogue, never a proposed Voynich vocabulary. It is fixed before new keys and messages. Character/letter-type doses4/3,21/13,61/20,138/26; genuine-final adversaries add a to every supplied word. No clue selected from the hidden message or for favorable outcome. The sampled doses do not establish a universal/minimal number of needed words.
hints.groups_false: Merge the first two chunks of the first eligible fit word, or split a lone chunk; ciphertext bytes unchanged.
hints.groups_noisy: Apply the same boundary corruption to a seeded10% sample of fit words; report actually changed count. Ciphertext unchanged.
hints.word26_wrong_pair: Exchange the cipher partners of the first two aligned reference words.
hints.word26_noisy: Change one leading ciphertext glyph of the last reference word to the next glyph modulo12; may leave an internally consistent but wrong code for a rare letter.
hints.word26_coherent_false: Exchange a/e throughout all26 supplied plaintext reference words. This can produce a perfectly consistent unique wrong codebook. A separate witness must reject it; internal fit and uniqueness alone are not sufficient.

independent_witness: A separate fixed nine-word pangram, the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog, has35 letters spanning all26. Its encoding is generated with the same hidden key and withheld from fitting. For genuine-final adversaries append a to each witness word too. Only after every rule is fixed, compare its literal decoding to this witness. Do not use witness to choose among multiple rules or repair a key. Count these9 known words in the information budget: richest condition uses26 fitting words plus9 checking words, not26 total. Witness coverage deliberately makes partial alphabet coverage insufficient for full verification. This is synthetic independence from fitting/message content, not external historical/human corroboration.
solver: Exhaustive finite word-equation backtracking over code lengths1..3, compatible common suffix lengths0..2, and directions+1/-1, with prefix-free injectivity. Deterministically choose next word by fewest unmapped letter types, most mapped occurrences, shortest plaintext, then input index. Stop at2 different models to certify ambiguity, or after all possibilities to establish uniqueness on covered letters. Uncovered letters remain undetermined. Limit2000000 recursion/parse nodes per condition; reaching limit never certifies uniqueness. Freeze all limits. Model scores and expected answers never rank alternatives.
release: Finish all fits first. Only a proved unique rule may be checked against the independent witness. If witness passes, decode fit and transfer unchanged; release only if both parse completely. No groups/answers from transfer enter fitting. An ambiguous condition is never promoted using witness or hidden truth. Fitter must not read sources, sealed answers, regression truths, or witness files. Full source integrity checking is performed separately.
metrics: Report each of34 cases times11 conditions, separating30 new cases from4 regressions. Distinguish released exact transfer, exact fit, full26-letter key/direction/padding recovery, unit identification, failed clue consistency, ambiguity, witness rejection, parsing abstention and resource limit. Count erroneous padding deletions at actual ciphertext glyph positions required by true plaintext. Report unique wrong rules before witness separately from false releases after witness. Grouping and plaintext information volumes use different units; do not claim equal-bit budgets or a universal information minimum.

gates.mechanical: Tiny alphabets compared to independent complete enumeration, positive toy inversion, ambiguity and resource-abstention checks must pass before new generation. Mechanical failure stops for diagnosis, no silent patch of frozen code.
gates.recovery: ALL20 new positives under correct26-word anchors must release exact transfer, correct units and complete actual rule. Preserve results for all lower doses, but do not choose a winner from them to replace this predefined gate.
gates.false_release: Zero incorrect released transfers or unit interpretations across ALL330 new case-condition records.
gates.false_hints: No release for any of five corrupted-hint conditions on any new case. Separately report inconsistencies versus ambiguities and rejection by witness. This gate is about these corruptions, not all possible misinformation.
gates.outside_model: No release in any condition for the8 outside-model cases.
gates.false_deletion: No glyph required for true plaintext may be removed by an operationally released padding rule. Includes12 no-null positives:8 digraph/variable literary controls and4 genuine-final adversaries.
gates.application: All computational gates AND an independently justified plaintext-to-cipher alignment with separate manuscript validation must be available. The pretrial evidence register currently has zero trusted historical pairs. No source-free inferred label or guessed month equivalence can substitute for that missing information.

manuscript: Do not run a key search on Voynich if gates/preconditions fail. Existing atlas and manuscript reserves have all been exposed. According to which hint proves useful, prepare a small critical-edition proposal and concurrent readings with falsifiable predictions, explicitly distinguishing transcription, alignment and meaning. No word is assumed translated. Paler or ambiguous signs retain alternatives. No human independent adjudication has occurred.
seeds: Four synthetic development families seed9, mechanical positive seed17. Literary case keys301000+100*source_index+10*pair_index+family_index; genuine-final302000+100*source_index+pair_index; Markov generation303000+source_index and encryption303100+source_index; boundary noise304000+opaque-case-index. Sources orderItalian,French; four regressions first; frozen generator defines subsequent ordering.
